issues.description: Transform is not applied to delimiter-split items, inconsistent with multi-instance/CSV paths
issues.detail: After splitting on delimiter, items is reassigned to a list of raw strings. The subsequent transform branch only runs when items is a list from the start; the new split path produces a list, so transform will apply, but the splitting also bypasses keep_blank_qs_values handling. Empty segments (e.g., 'a||b') yield '' entries even when blank values are normally dropped, which is inconsistent with existing behavior and undocumented beyond a brief note.

issues.description: Unsupported delimiter raises ValueError that escapes as 500 instead of HTTPBadRequest
issues.detail: get_param_as_list documents that ValueError from transforms is converted to HTTPBadRequest, but the new ValueError for an unsupported delimiter is raised before any transform and propagates as a server error. Since delimiter is developer-controlled this may be intentional, but it should be a programmer error (e.g., explicit TypeError or pre-validated) and documented in the Raises section.

issues.description: Default value for delimiter in overloads contradicts keyword-only stub semantics
issues.detail: The overload signatures specify `delimiter: str | None = None` as a default, but several overloads place it after `*,` keyword-only markers or after other defaulted params. Mixing literal defaults in overload stubs is fine, but the defaults differ from typical Falcon overload style (using `...`). This may confuse type checkers; verify mypy/pyright treat all six overloads consistently.

issues.description: Delimiter mapping permits redundant keys and conflates symbolic with literal
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS maps both literal characters and OAS symbolic names to the same set. This is fine but means an unsupported but reasonable delimiter (tab, semicolon) is rejected with no extension path. Consider documenting how to use arbitrary single-character delimiters, or accept any single character and only validate the symbolic names.

issues.description: Missing test for delimiter with transform callable
issues.detail: Tests cover delimiter splitting alone but never combine `delimiter=` with a `transform=` callable. Since the split items pass through the transform branch, a test confirming `get_param_as_list('ids', transform=int, delimiter='|')` works (and that a transform ValueError becomes HTTPBadRequest) would prevent regressions in the interaction.

issues.description: Docstring example shows percent-encoded pipe but no test asserts the docstring scenario
issues.detail: The doctest-style example in the docstring (`?colors=blue%7Cblack%7Cbrown` -> ['blue','black','brown']) is illustrative but not executed. Given the explicit note about percent-decoding ordering vs auto_parse_qs_csv, a doctest or a dedicated unit test mirroring the docstring would lock in that contract.

review.summary: The change is a clean, well-documented addition that maps a small set of OAS-aligned delimiters to split characters and only applies them when the param is a single string. Main concerns: a ValueError for an unknown delimiter will propagate as HTTP 500 due to the documented ValueError->HTTPBadRequest conversion only covering transform errors; delimiter splitting silently ignores keep_blank_qs_values for empty segments; and tests don't cover the delimiter+transform interaction. Overload defaults differ stylistically from existing patterns and warrant a mypy sanity check. Overall low-risk, P1 items are about edge-case correctness and error surface.
